facts.raw_span: A 17-year-old nulliparous female presented with a two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension
She denied pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms
her BMI was 20.5 kg/m2
blood pressure 125/85 mmHg
The abdomen was markedly distended with a palpable mass rising approximately 3 cm above the umbilicus
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile (MCV 73.2 fL)
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm
The lesion appeared unilocular with a 1.5 mm wall and no septations or solid components
The lesion was suggestive of an ovarian origin
There was no personal or family history of cancer
